title: Characterization Of Multi-layered Fish Scales (Atractosteus spatula) Using Nanoindentation, X-ray CT, FTIR, and SEM
protocol: Record the spatial location on the fish of the scales obtained for the study.
Store the scales in phosphate buffered saline solution to preserve hydration and maintain mineral content.
Use a medium bristle brush and tweezers to remove any soft tissue from the hard scales.
Mount the scale in a stiff medium such as a two-part epoxy consisting of a resin and hardener.
Ensure the epoxy has a peak temperature of less than 55 °C.
Hold the fish scale in a 32 mm diameter sample mold using a commercially available plastic sample holder.
Pour uncured epoxy on the sample and allow it to cure according to the manufacturer's directions.
Section the mounted sample using a diamond blade high-precision cut-off saw at the midline of the sample.
Sonicate the sample in distilled water for 15 min to remove debris.
Polish the sample to obtain a smooth flat surface.
Ultrasonicate samples in a bath of distilled water between polishing steps.
Coarse polish with a 15 µm SiC pad and water as a lubricant until the sample is plane using an automatic polishing head force of 7 lbf and speed of 200 revolutions per min (rpm).
Sonicate the sample in a bath of distilled water for 15 min.
Intermediate polish with a 6 µm SiC pad using water lubricant at a platen speed of 130 rpm and a force of 7 lbf for 5 min.
Sonicate the sample in a bath of distilled water for 15 min.
Polish with a 1 µm SiC pad using water lubricant at a platen speed of 130 rpm and a force of 7 lbf for 5 min.
Sonicate the sample in a bath of distilled water for 15 min.

Final polish with a 50 nm colloidal silica suspension using an appropriate polishing pad such as a high-density, non-woven, low-nap porous polyurethane that a manufacturer suggests for 50 nm suspensions.
Polish at a speed of 130 rpm with a force of 7 lbf for 5 min.
Sonicate the sample in a bath of distilled water for 15 min.
Calibrate the nanoindentation system before each batch of testing per the manufacturer’s guidelines.
Load the sample into the nanoindenter and use the optical microscope controls on the nanoindenter to bring the sample into focus.
Use software controls to move the specimen to the location for the first indent, approximately 10 µm in the epoxy from the edge of the ganoine layer along the centerline of the scale’s cross-section.
Perform 4 parallel rows of indents spaced 15 µm apart to obtain a statistically significant data set.
Set the nanoindenter to a maximum load of 5 mN, loading and unloading rates of 0.1 mN/sec, and a hold time of 30 sec.
Specify a minimum indent spacing of 5 µm for each row.
Run indents orthogonal to the ganoine surface, ensuring enough indents traverse approximately 10 µm into the epoxy past the bony layer.
Create fiducial indents with a maximum load of 100 mN at the first and last indent in the epoxy before the ganoine layer and after the bone layer, respectively.
Place the sample back in PBS solution to avoid further dehydration upon completion.
Use nanoindentation software to determine modulus and hardness based on the Oliver-Pharr method if a time-independent material response is observed.
Attach a slide-on ATR accessory to an FTIR microscope.
Prepare a fish scale sample with dimensions suitable for FTIR microscopy.
Ensure the surface of the sample is polished for high-quality spectra collection.
Calibrate the FTIR signal under the same conditions as will be used for measuring the sample.
Cool the detector and allow time for it to stabilize.
Collect background spectra in the absence of CO2 and water vapor interference.
Select an appropriate objective and focus on the area of interest within the sample.
Attach the ATR accessory to the FTIR microscope objective.
Raise the sample until it makes intimate contact with the ATR internal reflection element.
Collect a sample spectrum.
Perform standard data processing on the collected FTIR spectra.
Warm-up the X-ray source according to manufacturer’s specifications.
Set X-ray voltage and current to 50 kV and 160 µA, respectively.
Set exposure time to 1,450 msec.
Select a 1.0 mm aluminum filter.
Make a flat-field correction when the X-ray source is off (dark-field) and on (bright-field).
Mount scales in a manner so that they do not shift or move throughout the length of the scan.
Secure the scale to the CT stage using materials nearly transparent to X-rays, such as Styrofoam and Parafilm.
Rigidly mount the sample so that the longest dimension is parallel to the detector.
Secure the mounted sample to the scanner stage.
Position the sample so that it will be in the center of rotation throughout the scan.
Select the highest resolution that allows the entire scale to be in the field of view, in this case 7.5 µm.
Perform scans with a rotational step of 0.25°.
Set the frame averaging value to 15 for scans.
Reconstruct X-ray projection images using Skyscan’s NRecon software.
Change Ring Artifact Correction to 20 in reconstruction parameters.
Adjust Beam Hardening Correction to 25% in reconstruction settings.
Use CS Static Rotation adjustment to level cross-sectional images.
Obtain the final 3D gray-scale image with Skysan’s CTAn software.
Adjust the gray-scale range to remove artifacts from Styrofoam and Parafilm.
Place polished specimen into SEM chamber.
Pump chamber into low-vacuum mode with a pressure of 0.1 to 0.5 mbar.
Adjust working distance to approximately 5.0 mm.
Activate high voltage (HV).
Navigate to the region of interest on the specimen that includes the transition zone between ganoine and bony sublayers or other areas of interest.
Obtain images at 15 kV HV and a beam current of approximately 3.9 nA.
Focus image.
Perform all necessary alignments and stigmation adjustments.
Capture images from at least three regions of interest at relevant magnifications (typically 250X to 10,000X).
Use the low-vacuum backscattered electron (BSE) detector to aid in identification of changes in biomineral content and density.
Affix freshly fractured specimen to a 90° SEM stub using double-sided carbon tape with the fracture surface facing up.
Sputter coat with Au to provide a sub-nm thick conductive layer on the fracture surface.
Place specimen into SEM chamber and pump chamber into high-vacuum mode.
Adjust working distance to between 3.0 and 5.0 mm.
Activate HV and navigate to regions of interest on the specimen.
Obtain images at between 5 kV and 15 kV HV and a lower beam current of 0.24 nA.
Initially focus specimen and perform preliminary alignments.
Increase magnification to greater than 5,000X.
Switch from normal field emission lens into immersion/ultra-high resolution (UHR) lens.
Perform UHR alignments and stigmation adjustments.
Capture images from at least three regions of interest at relevant magnifications (typically 5,000X to 250,000X).
Use the through lens detector (TLD) operated in secondary electron (SE) mode.
Navigate to region of interest on polished specimen that includes nanoindentation grid indicated by fiducial marks at the end of each line of indents.
Ensure HV is at least 15 kV, beam current is at least 3.9 nA, and working distance is greater than 5.0 mm.
Capture BSE image of region to be analyzed using EDX.
Using EDX analysis software, capture the same image to aid in locating areas to perform chemical analysis along the line of indents.
Position a line to perform chemical analysis along the line of interest of indentations starting at the first indent and ending at the last indent.
Specify the number of analysis points to be placed along the line using the “Line Analysis” technique.
Initiate the line analysis using EDX software when the line is positioned and points are specified correctly.
Identify elements of interest to be quantified from the point spectra obtained along the specified line on the polished surface of the specimen.
Perform a background calibration to account for Bremsstrahlung radiation and other effects.
Choose the software’s deconvolution analysis option.
Obtain quantitative analysis on each point along the specified line.
Quantify the chemical composition at each point.
Save quantitative chemical analysis results.
Save an image of the specified line analyzed.
